 REDDING, Calif. — Halloween is upon us, and Mother Nature isn't exactly handing out treats locally. In fact, given how nice November looks to start out, this weather lands in the "trick" category without a doubt. 
 My weather themed pumpkin from 2025! We'll get a bit of all this over the weekend. (Preston Donion) 
 Showers associated with a low pressure system off the coast of Oregon will sweep into the region over the course of the day on Saturday, generally moving southwest to northeast. For folks on the North Coast, the wettest window will be 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., which isn't all bad -- we should be pretty dry in time for trick-or-treating! A little scattered drizzle later in the evening can't be ruled out, but that's a better outlook than most places. Communities throughout the valley are looking unlucky, with wet weather focusing in the 5 to 11 p.m. window. Cities in Shasta and Tehama County are likely to top the charts when it comes to rain totals, possibly exceeding a quarter of an inch in some spots. We may be able to stave off rain a smidge longer in Chico and Oroville than along I-5, but I wouldn't set your hopes too high for a dry trick-or-treating adventure anywhere in the lowlands. Across the mountains, showers look like more of a daylong nuisance. We could see scattered action even before the sun comes up, and rain continues in this off-and-on pattern all the way into early Sunday in some spots (especially areas east of I-5). There may be a brief window between rain bands around sunset in places like Burney and Chester, but "soggy" is still the overall theme of the night. 
 Precisioncast rain estimates through 4:30 p.m. Saturday. Valley communities should remain dry through this point, but not much longer! (KRCR) 
 Precisioncast rain estimates when all is said and done into Sunday morning. (KRCR) 
 Temperatures will run cool all day long but really dive into the evening. Expect valley cities to top out in the low 60s and slide back to the mid 50s by the time you're out and about in pursuit of king-size candy bars! In the higher terrain, low 50s are as warm as we can expect to get -- 40s are on tap in most spots in the hours after sunset. As you might imagine with a cool storm like this, winter weather is a possibility. Snow levels will drop as low as 5,500 feet as moisture exits the region, meaning light accumulations over eastern mountain peaks. Highway passes should stay wet and snow-free for the most part, but a brief "R1" chain restriction on Cedar Pass in Modoc County can't be ruled out on Sunday morning. 
 Precisioncast shows light snow over the eastern high country, with no major travel impacts but some nice new coats for peaks above 5500-6000 feet. (KRCR)PD10.png 
 So that covers the gnarly weather -- what about the nice part? That's where Sunday comes in! The storm will exit to the east overnight as we set our clocks back, giving way to largely sunny skies for the second half of the weekend. Temperatures rebound by a few degrees, meaning mid 60s in the valley and mainly mid 50s to about 60 in the higher terrain. Locally breezy north to northeast winds could show up in the valley and eastern foothills, but strong gusts are unlikely at this time. 
 Pleasant weather continues into the new week, with seasonable highs back through at least Election Day. Wednesday looks to mark the beginning of a new cooldown, and Thursday offers some shower potential. Keep an eye out for more details on this active week, and in the meantime, tune into our weekend weather broadcasts. You can also get up-to-the-minute weather information on the go by downloading the free KRCR Weather app from your device's app store!
